items.title: The induction step for a finitely presented flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the induction step of the flatterling theory over a finitely presented flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres: it produces a map from a finite free module to a finitely presented module that is an isomorphism on the special fibre, and shows that the flatness of the localisation at a prime over r is equivalent to five other conditions, one of which is the existence of localised elements making the map universally injective with flat cokernel (statement lines 3140-3169, tag 05IA). The proof constructs alpha from a basis of the fibre, then reduces the six conditions to one implication via the algebraic induction step, and that implication requires combining openness of the flat locus, openness of the isomorphism locus for a map of finitely presented modules, and openness of the image of a flat finitely presented ring map to produce the two localising elements. The openness argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
